newsitem.title: USA: IBM latest to arrive in crowded corp debt arena.
newsitem.headline: IBM latest to arrive in crowded corp debt arena.

text.p: The lure of cheaper financing amid a recent drop in long-term U.S. interest rates has drawn International Business Machines Corp into a crowded corporate debt arena, dealer said.
The computer and software maker is expected to issue $500 million in 10-year noncallable debt and $500 million in 30-year debt, putable in the seventh year, dealers said.
Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is expected to underwrite the offering, they said.
IBM is the latest in a string of U.S. corporations to capitalize on falling interest rates to finance debt.
Price talk on the 10-year issue is seen in the low 40 basis points over Tresuries area and between 18-20 basis points over for the 30-year issue, players said.
"At the current levels, we continue to see more and more surprise deals as issuers take advantage of cheaper financing levels," said one syndicate source.
Currently, the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond remains below the 6.50 percent level, at 6.33 percent; falling to its lowest level since 6.34 percent in March, 1996.
